card: Bumps the minimum supported Clang version from 17.0 to 19.0 in CMake, CI, and documentation. This enables the use of C++20 CTAD for alias templates and cleans up obsolete compiler workarounds in CMake and tests. Developers building with older Clang versions will need to upgrade or switch to GCC.
changed_since_previous: Added commits removing an obsolete clang-17 `-Wno-c++23-extensions` flag in CMakeLists.txt and an unused Windows include in src/compat/byteswap.h.
evidence: PR description notes: 'Most supported operating systems ship with clang-19 (or later), so bump the minimum to that and allow new code to drop workarounds for previous clang bugs. (For this bump, only C++20 CTAD will become available.)'
PR description lists default Clang packages across supported operating systems confirming Clang 19 availability.
problem: Supporting Clang 17 and 18 prevents adopting C++20 CTAD for alias templates and requires retaining compiler-specific workarounds and warning suppressions across the codebase and build system.

risk.why: A mistake would cause build failures on systems with older or specific Clang installations, which would be immediately caught in CI and by developers.

summary: Bumps the minimum required Clang compiler version from 17.0 to 19.0 across CMake checks, CI environments, and documentation. It updates CMake to enforce C++20 Class Template Argument Deduction (CTAD) for alias templates, sets clang-format to the latest standard, and drops obsolete workarounds for Clang 17 and libc++ 16.
